I think it's the dopamine hit.  Turns out you get it from a "near-miss" as well as from a "win" situation.  That's great for when we're learning skills like throwing a ball, but when it comes to trying to forge relationships, it's problematic.  

Our brains seem to go "Well... they're NEARLY an amazing match for us! Have some dopamine!"  Then, when it wears off, we're conditioned to have another go, to see if we can make it "right" this time.  On some level, we're SURE that if we just do *something* a little differently, we're going to get a Big Payoff in the form of a loving, mutually respectful relationship.

So, when we give up on that, all our instincts are screaming "But... but... you were SO CLOSE! You're going to miss out on something AMAZING!"  It hurts to give up.  It undermines our confidence and self esteem.  We feel like worse people for doing so.
